title: p5.js 2.x Migration Mapper
description: A code-conversion exercise in which learners flag the v1-only call in four short p5.js 1.x snippets (preload, multi-control-point bezierVertex, curveVertex, quadraticVertex), choose its replacement from three candidates, and compare their version with the corrected 2.x form, with feedback quoting the Chapter 5 migration table.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: p5.js
Library Version Migration
Library Version Drift
MicroSim Maintenance
publisher: MicroSims 2.0: Generating, Instrumenting and Evaluating Interactive Learning Objects with AI

learningObjectives: The learner will use the migration table to convert a short p5.js 1.x snippet into its 2.x form and identify which call in it is no longer valid.
prerequisites: Library version drift and the p5.js 2.x migration table (Chapter 5)
Reading a p5.js sketch with beginShape() and endShape() (Chapter 6)

controls.label: Flag legacy calls
controls.action: Highlight the lines that use a v1-only call and name the call

controls.label: Show 2.x form
controls.action: Reveal the corrected snippet with changed lines highlighted

canvasInteractions: Click a highlighted line to open three candidate replacements
Click a candidate to choose it
Hover a call chip to read its migration rule

assumptions: Each snippet contains exactly one kind of v1-only call
Rules follow the Chapter 5 migration table and the p5.js 2.x reference

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked-example completion with explanatory feedback quoting the reference table
keyQuestions: Which call in this snippet is no longer valid in p5.js 2.x?
What does the migration table say replaces it?
Why is renaming alone not always enough?
commonMisconceptions: bezierVertex() keeps its six-number form in 2.x
Renaming curveVertex() to splineVertex() is the whole migration
assessmentOpportunities: First-try correct conversions out of four
Written 2.x form of a new 1.x snippet
